title: Vitable Health and SYNERGY HomeCare Partner to Support Caregivers
summary: Vitable Health is now a preferred partner for SYNERGY HomeCare, delivering flexible, affordable benefits that caregivers can actually use.
body_text: Vitable Health is proud to be a partner for SYNERGY HomeCare , one of the nation’s leading providers of in-home care. Together, we share a mission to support the caregivers who dedicate their lives to helping seniors and families remain safe and independent at home. This collaboration is already making an impact, with multiple SYNERGY locations across the country now offering Vitable Health’s flexible, affordable benefits to their teams. Caregiving is essential work, but too often caregivers struggle to access health coverage that truly works for them. Through this partnership, SYNERGY HomeCare agencies can offer a smarter alternative—health benefits that caregivers actually use. By providing coverage that is simple, affordable, and built around everyday health needs, we’re setting a new standard for caregiver support. Supporting Caregivers with Smarter Benefits Every Vitable Health plan is designed with primary care at the center, ensuring caregivers can access care without financial barriers. For SYNERGY HomeCare, our partnership has focused on the following benefit options: Virtual Primary Care (VPC) : Unlimited $0 virtual visits for everyday health needs, including primary and urgent care consultations, prescriptions, lab testing, and mental health coaching. Caregivers can connect with medical providers quickly and easily, ensuring they get the support they need without worrying about co-pays or deductibles. ‍ Individual Coverage Health Reimbursement Arrangement (ICHRA) : A flexible, tax-advantaged solution that allows employers to reimburse employees for individual health insurance plans, giving caregivers more choice in coverage. ‍ Minimum Essential Coverage (MEC) : A simple, compliant solution for meeting ACA requirements. MEC plans allow SYNERGY agencies to provide the necessary coverage and documentation, such as IRS reporting support, while keeping costs predictable and manageable. ‍ Occupational Health Services: Practical support for agencies, including TB testing and other compliance-focused services that help caregivers stay work-ready and safe. Beyond these core offerings, Vitable Health also provides a range of other options, including Minimum Value Plans (MVP), dental, and vision benefits, ensuring each SYNERGY HomeCare agency can select a benefits package that fits its budget and team’s needs. The flexibility to mix and match benefits means agencies can scale their offerings while keeping administration simple. Why This Partnership Matters For caregivers, these benefits mean more than just healthcare—they mean peace of mind. Having access to care that is convenient and affordable helps caregivers stay healthier, more engaged, and more committed to their work. For SYNERGY franchise owners, offering Vitable Health plans supports recruitment and retention in an industry where high turnover is common. As one SYNERGY owner put it, Vitable Health delivered the affordability and trust of a franchise-preferred partner while giving his employees and family access to high-quality care that felt like a full health plan—without the cost and limitations of traditional options. “It’s been one of the smartest investments we've made for our employees and our business,” says Ken Gregson, owner SYNERGY HomeCare of Bradenton. A Shared Commitment to Care The preferred partnership between Vitable Health and SYNERGY HomeCare is about more than compliance—it’s about compassion. By investing in caregivers’ health, SYNERGY HomeCare is demonstrating its commitment not only to the clients it serves but also to the teams who make that care possible. We’re excited to continue expanding our partnership across the SYNERGY network, bringing better healthcare benefits to more caregivers nationwide. Because when we care for the caregiver, everyone benefits.

title: Back-to-School Budgeting Tips for Families
summary: Back-to-school time means back to the store for supplies, clothes, new tech, & even budgeting for food and activities.
body_text: Back-to-School Budgeting Tips for Families Back-to-school time means back to the store for supplies, clothes, new tech, and even budgeting for food and activities as the kids head out of the house for another year. Excitement is high but so is stress for overwhelmed families managing their finances. At Landmark National Bank, our online banking tools help you take control of your money to reach your budgeting goals in times of increased spending. From organizing shopping lists to tracking your spending, a little planning goes a long way when it comes to hitting your budget. Let’s look at a few practical ways to save money during back-to-school season. How to set a realistic back-to-school budget It’s easy to hit the store (or a website) and leave with hundreds of dollars of unnecessary items. Budgeting success begins by being precise with your shopping and knowing exactly what you need, what you intend to buy, and sticking to your list. To start, make a list of “must have” items your child will need as they head back to school. For example “clothes, school supplies, and accessories such as a new water bottle.” Next, set a budget for each item on your list. If you don’t intend to spend more than sixty dollars on new clothes, note that on your list. As you go about your shopping, in- store or online, hold fast and don’t go over your set budget. Don’t forget about recurring school expenses like lunch money, extracurricular fees, sports gear, and school photos. These smaller costs can add up quickly if they’re not factored into your initial budget. Try setting aside a small amount each month to cover school expenses each year. Consider moving the money to a personal savings account, so it’s always there when you need it. Evaluate your list Now that you have your list of back-to-school items, do a thorough evaluation of what you may already have before you head out to the store. There may be existing school supplies piled up in the basement or hand-me-down clothes you could pass down from one sibling to another, bypassing the need for additional cost. Money saving tip: Gather gently used clothes your child has outgrown and take them to a resale shop, adding money to your back-to-school budget. Money-saving tips List in hand, you’re almost ready to head out the door and shop for your back-to-school items. First, look for deals and sales to help make your dollar go further. Here are a few ways to help you find cost-savings. Shop stores like Costco or Sam’s Club to gain savings on bulk items. Search for resale items on sites like eBay or Facebook Marketplace or even second hand stores. Ask friends about “swapping” items and clothing, passing down clothing from younger to older kids for money-savings and sustainability. Keep an eye out for “tax free weekends” and watch for coupons in the newspaper or online. Financial calculators help track your budget Staying on budget is easier with the help of tools like financial calculators or simple budgeting worksheets to help you chart your progress. At Landmark National Bank, we have a suite of digital, financial calculators within our online banking tools to help you take control of your personal finances and stay within your budget. Plan to stay on budget all year long As the school year begins, look ahead to the full year of expenses. Go back through last year’s calendar and see what and where you spent money throughout the year. (ie. Halloween costumes, Christmas presents for teachers, etc). Make a budgeting calendar, planning for school expenses each month, so you’ll be prepared and have money set aside when the time comes. Involve the kids in budgeting and money decisions Creating healthy financial behaviors starts by inviting kids into budgeting decisions early to help them understand the value of money. Take the list you’ve created so far and sit down with your child, telling them how much money is in your back-to-school budget and let them make a few adjustments, allowing for things they want or may not need. That way, kids feel a part of the process and may even contribute some of their own money or ideas for back-to-school budgeting. For all of your family financial planning Whether it’s online, over the phone, or in person, we’re here to help you manage your personal and family finance s. With personal support, honest guidance, and real conversations, we help you make confident financial decisions every day. Reach out to a Landmark National Bank team member if you’d like help walking through your back-to-school budget. And don’t forget to subscribe to the blog for tips on managing your money and all of your online banking needs.

title: What does protein powder do?
summary: Learn what protein powder does, its top benefits for muscle growth, weight loss, recovery, and how it supports your daily nutrition and fitness goals.
body_text: What does protein powder do? Written by: Sarah Oliver | Published on August 13, 2025 | Time to read 1 min What Protein Powder Do? What is protein? Protein is one of three macronutrients your body needs daily, and in large amounts, and they provide the energy needed for bodily functions. The other two macronutrients are fat and carbohydrates, but for the purpose of this article we will focus on protein and protein powder as a supplement. Protein is made up of smaller building blocks called amino acids. There are 20 amino acids, and the human body is capable of producing 11 of these on their own. The remaining 9 amino acids (called essential amino acids) need to be consumed through the foods we consume as the human body is unable to produce them. The 9 essential amino acids are: Phenylalanine Valine Threonine Tryptophan Methionine Leucine Isoleucine Lysine Histidine The role of protein in the human body is extremely varied but includes important functions such as: Repairing and building tissue Making enzymes and hormones Supporting the strong and healthy structure of bones, hair, skin, muscles, and other tissues While protein is not the primary energy source for humans (carbohydrates and fats take the top two spots for this) - it can be used as a last resort in a process known as gluconeogenesis. Gluconeogenesis is a metabolic process that results in the formation of glucose from a non-carbohydrate substrate (such as a protein); this means that protein and turn into a source of fuel for athletes completing strenuous activity. So what about protein powder? Protein powder is a popular nutritional supplement that gives users all the benefits of protein in a cost effective, and convenient way. Not to mention that there are many ways that one can make their protein shake delicious. The specific use case of protein powder will come down to the individual user and can include cases such as: muscle growth and recovery, weight loss, added nutrition, sports performance, among others. There are also many types of protein powders that can also be used in different ways for different use cases. Some types of protein includes: whey protein, casein, pea protein, and brown rice protein. ← Go back

title: SRE.ai Raises $7.2M To Redefine Enterprise DevOps for the AI Era
body_text: It’s no secret that enterprise DevOps hasn’t kept up with how businesses actually run today. Platforms like Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Workday have become mission-critical, but traditional DevOps and Reliability tools were never built for them. But maybe the solution isn’t just more tools. Maybe it’s a DevOps layer designed for these platforms from the ground up. That’s exactly what we’re building at SRE.ai , starting with Salesforce . Before SRE.ai, my cofounder and I spent years at Google DeepMind and Google Translate, building AI systems that required rigor, scale, and resilience. We saw firsthand that systems built on solid foundations, not patched together reactively, are the ones that last. SRE.ai brings that same engineering-grade approach to Salesforce DevOps. Instead of treating it like a second-class citizen, we provide an AI-native control plane that: Detects and prevents risky changes before they break production Orchestrates release cycles across teams and business units Answers plain-language questions like “What changed in the last release that could affect our quoting process?” with contextual, actionable insights Reduces chaos and tribal knowledge, letting teams move faster and more confidently While Salesforce is our initial focus, the same approach applies to other enterprise systems like Workday and ServiceNow platforms that often suffer from the same complexity and risk. Still, we’re starting where the need is clearest. Early users confirmed what we suspected: Salesforce teams want an AI-native layer that remembers, orchestrates, and scales their DevOps processes. We’re grateful for the support of Salesforce Ventures, Y Combinator, Crane Venture Partners, and our incredible angel investors , who share our vision for the next generation of enterprise DevOps. This is just the start. If you’re working with Salesforce and want to see AI-native DevOps in action, come try SRE.ai today. {{image_1}}
